At dusk, shared rules for hand-off notes
This section explains the main rule first, then the reasons

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: This section sets the standard for calm, accurate handling of animal travel requests so passengers, pets, and airport teams receive steady support.

The main rule is that every interaction must protect animal welfare, preserve clear records, and keep the passenger informed in plain language. Staff members should listen with care, confirm the travel plan, and note any comfort needs without delay. If a passenger appears worried, the response must remain patient and respectful, and the concern should be shared with the senior coordinator as needed. The welfare coordinator reviews animal comfort needs and may request added checks, alternate handling steps, or a more detailed hand-off note. Staff should never promise an arrangement that has not been approved through the proper review.

When preparing a hand-off, use the approved desk format and include only relevant facts about the animal, the carrier, and any special handling. Keep notes concise, factual, and free of casual wording. If there is confusion in the booking record, pause the exchange and verify the details before continuing. Supervisors listen carefully when a passenger is worried, and staff should follow the same attentive standard at the desk. If a traveler such as Layla Torres or Naomi Kowalski raises a concern about a pet such as Hazel, the matter should be acknowledged at once and routed through the correct internal channel.

Courtesy must remain constant during busy periods, because a calm tone reduces stress for both passengers and animals. The desk should also keep all shared information secure and avoid repeating private details beyond the staff who need them for service delivery. If a case falls outside normal practice, staff must escalate it promptly and wait for direction before proceeding.

For further guidance, contact the senior coordinator or the welfare coordinator through the usual internal channel.
